regionRelationship.summary: A repaired civic frontier immediately beyond Skyhome’s inhabited wall districts, where old fortress infrastructure meets the unstable approaches to the First Gate.
regionRelationship.administrativeStatus: Shared civic work zone under Skyhome review; no Founder or Guildmaster owns the land or its people.
regionRelationship.guildMandate: The new guild handles rescue, survey, escort, anomaly containment, contract mediation, and threats too small or scattered for standing civic forces but too dangerous for ordinary workers.

visualIdentity.silhouetteLanguage: Massive incomplete arches, repaired bridges, pulley cranes, scaffold towers, conduit ribs, and temporary homes built against architecture older than current memory.
environmentalStorytelling: Old kill-zones have become kitchens, clinics, and tool depots.
Former enemy warning symbols are overwritten by multilingual civic directions rather than erased.
Fresh repairs use visible mixed-race techniques so cooperation is literally built into the walls.
Unclaimed rooms still contain pre-Forgetting maintenance marks whose purpose is not understood.
Children paint route colors on stones while surveyors argue over whether the gate is waking or remembering.
visualIdentity.boardGameLanguage: An illustrated raised-relief expedition board: route cords illuminate between large encounter spaces; node cards feel like stamped guild records placed over a living map.
visualIdentity.combatArenaLanguage: Compact tactical arenas built from work platforms, broken arches, relief roads, suspended chains, salvage stacks, and active gate conduits. Objectives and hazards are visually readable before forecasts are chosen.

architecture.name: Gate Ribs
architecture.use: Ancient curved supports that hum during anomalies; create cover, elevation, and Arcana checks.

architecture.name: Repair Walks
architecture.use: Modular bridges and scaffold lanes used by workers; can collapse, reroute, or become escort objectives.

architecture.name: Relief Arches
architecture.use: Converted checkpoints providing food, medicine, and contract witnesses.

architecture.name: Winch Towers
architecture.use: Goblin and human rebuilt cranes used for salvage, traversal, and environmental combat actions.

architecture.name: World Markers
architecture.use: Stone-and-brass survey posts recording gate pulses, routes, and cultural boundaries.

architecture.name: Old Service Walls
architecture.use: Thick maintenance partitions containing ordinary secrets and, for authorized profiles only, a noncanonical Margin entrance.

weatherProfiles.description: Cold blue wind carries distant gate chimes.
Metal-rich condensation falls from ancient ribs and makes walkways slick.
Brief visible currents interfere with spell shaping and awaken constructs.
Repair dust and wind reduce sight lines.
Worker lanterns form islands of warmth against gate-blue darkness.

musicDirection.exploration: Measured hand percussion, hammered dulcimer, low strings, distant metallic gate tones, and hopeful woodwinds that enter near civic spaces.
musicDirection.danger: Irregular chain percussion and reversed gate chimes without losing the human worker rhythm.
musicDirection.boss: The worker rhythm becomes the tactical pulse; the gate motif fragments among enemy Unions and resolves only when support pylons are silenced.

inhabitantGroups.storyUse: Witnesses, rescue targets, assistants, and source of practical events.
Civic stakes and relationship events; never generic loot dispensers.
Trade, rivalry, fraud, and recovery contracts.
Early hints that the Gateworks belongs to more than one people.
Tutorial and persistence support without replacing random recruits.

wildlife.behavior: Harmless unless drawn into an active conduit.
Nest in warm gate seams and reveal weather shifts.
Normally docile pack animals; panic around broken signals.

factions.name: Broken Charter Crew
factions.motive: Control valuable salvage routes and hide earlier contract failures; members can retreat, bargain, or reform.

factions.name: Awakened Maintenance Network
factions.motive: Ancient systems interpret current repairs as contamination and attempt to restore an obsolete defensive state.

factions.name: Gate-Touched Predators
factions.motive: Animals and growths displaced or altered by gate pulses; not uniformly evil.

mysteries: The gate sometimes rings once for people who have never crossed it.
Maintenance diagrams depict roads into worlds with erased names.
Some wall repairs are newer than Skyhome records but use no known tools.
The First Gate responds differently to mixed-race Unions than to isolated groups.
ordinarySecretLanguage: All-player secrets use visible world logic: mismatched mortar, airflow, scent, old survey codes, breakable braces, and solvable terminals.
marginTreatment: The authorized Margin appears as a clean page-shaped absence behind an ordinary service wall. Local textures continue around it but do not enter it; sound drops to a paper-soft hush. This presentation is explicitly noncanon and unavailable to normal profiles.
storyBoundaries: The guild serves Skyhome; it does not replace civic institutions or Founder authority.
The zone may foreshadow gates and the Great Forgetting but cannot reveal protected final answers.
Kael and the Seven Founders may be referenced as public figures but do not become owned applicants or routine tutorial companions.
Residents retain agency; rescue does not imply ownership, debt bondage, or forced recruitment.
futureHooks: Gate pulse patterns that match another world
A missing maintenance route beneath the First Gate
A Broken Charter survivor seeking lawful appeal
A nonhostile creature carrying an ancient route token
Evidence that the awakened network is obeying a damaged instruction rather than malice
